AC-01: validate protected requirement — In production, when `x-vercel-oidc-token` is absent and `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` contains a valid bounded token, `runtime_vercel_oidc_token(...)` returns that environment token for server-side provider composition.
AC-02: validate protected requirement — A valid `x-vercel-oidc-token` value takes precedence over `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, preserving explicit request-scoped runtime identity when available.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Production with neither a valid request token nor a valid environment token raises `ProductionDeliveryConfigurationError`. Malformed, whitespace-padded, control-character, too-short, or oversized values are not accepted.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Non-production callers with no valid runtime token continue to return `None`; this fix does not inject production provider authority into local/Preview execution.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — No new long-lived GitHub/Vercel/QA secret is introduced. The resolved value remains server-owned Vercel deployment identity and is not persisted or exposed.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The Vercel OIDC token can only reach GitHub through the existing Connect exchange and exact repository-scope verification. Project/repository mismatch and provider authorization failures still fail closed.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — After exact API deployment, the QA-owned canonical Engineering Run can retry from PLAN without `CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` at `provider-repository`. If a later independent failure occurs, it is recorded separately and is not relabeled as a pass.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Only after AC-07 is proven may the same QA-owned run be reconsidered as a valid W8-S2 canonical equivalent. W8-S2 passes only if it durably advances beyond the former missing-static-target PLAN failure without `ProductionDeliveryConfigurationError` caused by static Preview-target registration.

critique: The production runtime environment credential `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` is missing and the `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` value is valid. The resolved Vercel OIDC token is accepted only through the same bearer validation used for request-scoped values. The environment value is accepted only through the same bounded bearer validation used for request-scoped values. Missing or malformed production runtime OIDC still fails closed with `ProductionDeliveryConfigurationError`. No client-supplied bearer header, cookie, QA credential, Supabase credential, GitHub personal token, reusable GitHub secret, database field, or service-role token is added. The resolved Vercel OIDC remains an input only to the existing `VercelConnectGitHubCredentialProvider`, which must still obtain and verify an exact repository-scoped GitHub App installation credential. Existing Project ownership checks, `ToolCapabilityRegistry`, provider action authorization, repository binding, source-lineage validation, dynamic Vercel Project readiness, Preview-only deployment, pull-request delivery, and REVIEW completion authority remain unchanged.
